description: Films with a replacement cost equal to 20.99 are included along with those above it.

d.request: Films with replacement_cost >= 20.99 are grouped by original_language_id (NULL forming its own group), showing each group's original_language_id, the unrounded average of rental_rate / rental_duration, and the film count, ordered by film count descending (NULL counts last), top 10 only.
d.sql: SELECT original_language_id, AVG(rental_rate * 1.0 / rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_day, COUNT(*) AS film_count FROM film WHERE replacement_cost >= 20.99 GROUP BY original_language_id ORDER BY film_count DESC, CASE WHEN original_language_id IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, original_language_id LIMIT 10

b.request: Group films with replacement_cost >= 20.99 by original_language_id (NULL as its own group), and for each group show the original_language_id, the unrounded average of rental_rate/rental_duration (ignoring NULLs), and the film count, ordered by film count descending with NULL counts last, limited to the top 10.
b.sql: SELECT original_language_id, AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_day, COUNT(*) AS film_count FROM film WHERE replacement_cost >= 20.99 GROUP BY original_language_id ORDER BY film_count DESC LIMIT 10
b.raw: Group films with replacement_cost >= 20.99 by original_language_id (NULL as its own group), and for each group show the original_language_id, the unrounded average of rental_rate/rental_duration (ignoring NULLs), and the film count, ordered by film count descending with NULL counts last, limited to the top 10.

c.request: Using 20.99 as the replacement-cost cutoff for films, group the qualifying films by `original_language_id`, with films that have no original language forming their own group. For each group, show the original language id, the average of `rental_rate` divided by `rental_duration` across its films (unrounded, ignoring missing values), and the number of films. Sort the groups from most films to fewest (any missing counts last) and show only the top 10. Films with a replacement cost equal to 20.99 are included along with those above it.
c.sql: SELECT original_language_id, AVG(rental_rate * 1.0 / rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_day, COUNT(*) AS film_count FROM film WHERE replacement_cost >= 20.99 GROUP BY original_language_id ORDER BY film_count DESC LIMIT 10

a.request: Considering only films whose replacement cost is at least 20.99, group them by `original_language_id`, with films that have no original language forming their own group. For each group, show the original language id, the average of `rental_rate` divided by `rental_duration` across its films (unrounded, ignoring missing values), and the number of films. Sort the groups from most films to fewest (any missing counts last) and show only the top 10.
a.sql: SELECT original_language_id, AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_day, COUNT(*) AS film_count FROM film WHERE replacement_cost >= 20.99 GROUP BY original_language_id ORDER BY film_count DESC LIMIT 10
